title: Beef and Vegetables without Carrots, Broccoli, Dark‑Green Leafy Greens

content.title: About
content.content: Thinly sliced beef is quickly stir‑fried with a mix of vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, cauliflower and onion, deliberately omitting carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens and potatoes. No soy‑based sauce is used, making the dish suitable for those avoiding soy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef provides highly bioavailable iron compared with plant sources.
Bell pepper and zucchini are rich in vitamin C, which enhances iron absorption from meat.
Skipping soy sauce reduces added glutamate, a common flavor enhancer.
High‑heat stir‑frying locks in beef juiciness while keeping vegetables crisp.
The recipe can be customized with different spices—cumin, paprika, ginger—to suit various cuisines.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef supplies complete animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support immune function and hemoglobin formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is a good source of vitamin B12 for nervous system health and niacin for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Vitamin C and carotenoids in bell pepper and zucchini help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Excluding potatoes and carrots makes the dish suitable for low‑carb eating patterns.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Large portions of beef can raise cholesterol levels; choose lean cuts when possible.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Overcooking vegetables
items.content: Excessive stir‑frying can degrade vitamins and create harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice beef thinly, stir‑fry on high heat for 2‑3 minutes, then add the vegetables (bell pepper, zucchini, cauliflower, onion). Season with salt, pepper and your favorite spices. Cook, stirring, until vegetables are tender‑crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of water or broth to restore moisture.
